title: River family reappearance had a positive link to past nearby detections but no clear time-direction signal
abstract: We tested whether nearby family detections precede local reappearance in English river invertebrates. ChemPop version 2.0 supplied 41,209 risk records at 169 sites for 79 family labels in 1996-2016. Reappearance followed two zero-detection years. The joint model used family-site, family-year and site-year effects, local detection history, and matched donor coverage for past and future supply. A 0.10 increase in past nearby detection frequency had a 1.72 percentage point link to reappearance (95% interval 0.52-2.92). The future link was 0.98 points (-0.07-2.03). Their difference was 0.73 (-0.65-2.11), with site, family and year cluster uncertainty. Kernel changes and removal of history kept uncertain time-direction contrasts. Thus a positive source marker did not identify a clear past-future separation in this river test. The intervals do not show equal effects or no dispersal. Family detection, Euclidean distance, selected histories and unmeasured local conditions limit causal use. The study does not measure the share of the thermal gap due to dispersal. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and external-data regeneration instructions are included.

display.caption: Past, future and past-minus-future nearby detection links to annual river family reappearance. Bars give nominal three-way cluster 95% intervals. The right panel changes the kernel scale on the same records.
